questions.question: A number line runs from 30 000 to 40 000. It is divided into 10 equal parts, so each part is worth 1000. A dot sits exactly on the 6th mark after 30 000. Round the number at the dot to the nearest ten thousand.
questions.explain: The dot is at 30 000 + 6 × 1000 = 36 000. To round to the nearest ten thousand, ask which end of the line it is closer to: 36 000 is past the halfway mark 35 000, so it rounds up to 40 000. The usual trap is rounding at the thousands place instead and leaving 36 000.

questions.question: A number line runs from 200 000 to 300 000. It is split into 10 equal parts, so each part is worth 10 000. A dot sits exactly on the 3rd mark after 200 000. Round the number at the dot to the nearest hundred thousand.
questions.explain: The dot is at 200 000 + 3 × 10 000 = 230 000. Rounding to the nearest hundred thousand means choosing the closer end of the line: 230 000 is below the halfway mark 250 000, so it rounds down to 200 000. Many children round up just because the line ends at 300 000.

questions.question: A number line runs from 0 to 1 000 000 and is divided into 10 equal parts, so each part is worth 100 000. A dot sits exactly halfway between the mark at 700 000 and the mark at 800 000. Round the number at the dot to the nearest hundred thousand.
questions.explain: Halfway between 700 000 and 800 000 is 750 000, and a number exactly on the halfway mark rounds up, giving 800 000. The trap is rounding at the millions place instead and jumping all the way to 1 000 000.

questions.question: A number line runs from 480 000 to 490 000. It is divided into 10 equal parts, so each part is worth 1000. A dot sits exactly on the 7th mark after 480 000. Round the number at the dot to the nearest ten thousand.
questions.explain: The dot is at 480 000 + 7 × 1000 = 487 000. The halfway point of this line is 485 000, and 487 000 is past it, so to the nearest ten thousand it is 490 000. Watch out for rounding at the hundred thousands place, which would wrongly give 500 000.

questions.question: Round 348 726 to the nearest ten thousand.
questions.explain: Find the ten thousands digit (4), then look at the digit just to its right, the thousands digit 8. Since 8 is 5 or more, the 4 goes up to 5 and every digit after it becomes 0, giving 350 000. The common slip is rounding at a different place, such as the thousands place, which gives 349 000.

questions.question: A BC ferry company carried 254 890 passengers last summer. A newspaper headline needs this number rounded to the nearest hundred thousand. What should the headline say?
questions.explain: For the nearest hundred thousand, look at the hundred thousands digit (2) and the digit right after it, the ten thousands digit 5. Since 5 is 5 or more, round up to 300 000. Rounding at the ten thousands place instead gives 250 000, which is the most common mistake here.

questions.question: Which number becomes 700 000 when it is rounded to the nearest hundred thousand?
questions.explain: To round to the nearest hundred thousand, check the ten thousands digit. In 682 300 that digit is 8, so 6 hundred thousands rounds up to 700 000. Numbers such as 751 000 and 769 400 have a 5 or 6 in the ten thousands place, so they round up to 800 000 instead — do not judge by the leading digit alone.

questions.question: A Surrey school orders paper in boxes. One box holds about 1000 sheets — that is the benchmark. The storage room has 48 boxes. About how many sheets are there, rounded to the nearest ten thousand?
questions.explain: First estimate with the benchmark: 48 × 1000 = 48 000 sheets. Then round 48 000 to the nearest ten thousand — the thousands digit is 8, so it rounds up to 50 000. Stopping at 48 000 means the rounding step to the asked place was never done.

questions.question: Liam rounded 467 851 to the nearest ten thousand and wrote 460 000. What went wrong, and what is the correct answer?
options: He should look at the digit just to the right of the ten thousands place, the thousands digit 7; since 7 is 5 or more, the answer is 470 000.
He should look at the ten thousands digit itself, 6, which is more than 5, so the answer is 500 000.
He should look at the hundreds digit, 8, so the answer is 467 900.
questions.explain: To round to a given place, keep your eye on the place you are rounding to, then check only the single digit to its right. Here the ten thousands digit is 6 and the digit to its right is 7, so round up to 470 000. Liam rounded in the wrong direction by ignoring that 7.

questions.question: The Vancouver Aquarium sold 187 400 tickets in the summer and 96 300 tickets in the fall. To estimate the total, round each number to the nearest ten thousand first, then add. What is the estimate?
questions.explain: Round each number at the ten thousands place: 187 400 becomes 190 000 (the thousands digit 7 rounds up) and 96 300 becomes 100 000 (the thousands digit 6 rounds up), so the estimate is 290 000. Rounding 96 300 down to 90 000 is the usual error and gives 280 000.

questions.question: An Okanagan orchard packs apples into crates that each hold about 2000 apples — that is the benchmark. A truck is loaded with 43 crates. Estimate the number of apples on the truck, rounded to the nearest ten thousand.
questions.explain: Use the benchmark first: 43 × 2000 = 86 000 apples. Then round at the ten thousands place — the thousands digit is 6, so 80 000 goes up to 90 000. Rounding at the hundred thousands place instead would wrongly give 100 000.

questions.question: A Kelowna news site reported that about 600 000 people visited a provincial park last year. The reporter rounded the exact number to the nearest hundred thousand. Which of these could be the exact number?
questions.explain: A number rounds to 600 000 at the hundred thousands place only if it sits between 550 000 and 650 000, and 649 200 does. Checking a digit further to the right, such as the thousands digit, is the usual trap: it makes 652 700 look like it rounds down when it really rounds to 700 000.
